scenes.narration: If your one gateway fails, everyone loses the internet. That's a big problem. H S R P keeps a spare ready to step in.

scenes.heading: Captain and first officer
scenes.narration: A plane has two pilots, but only one flies at a time. The captain is the active router. The first officer is the standby. Air traffic control uses one call sign, and that's the virtual I P address. If the captain can't fly, the first officer takes over. And the call sign never changes, so nobody notices.

scenes.heading: Setting it up
scenes.narration: Give the group a virtual I P. Set a priority, where higher wins. And turn on preempt, because it's off by default. Then check with show standby brief.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three slip-ups. H S R P Hellos come from the real address, not the virtual one. H S R P is active standby, so it doesn't load balance by default. And only the active router answers A R P for the virtual address.

items.wrong: Hellos come from the virtual IP
items.right: They use the real interface IP

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. H S R P gives hosts one gateway that never goes down. Highest priority wins, default is one hundred. Remember to turn on preempt. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva HSRP lab.

points.t: One virtual gateway that survives failure
